## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 2, titled *Dutiyaparimaṇḍala* ("Not wearing the upper robe evenly all around"), is the second training rule in the *sekhiya* (etiquette) section of the Vinaya Piṭaka's Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates monastic deportment, requiring monks to wrap the upper monastic robe evenly all around the body [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali available on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral records extensive cross-tradition parallels for the rule, including the Pali Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (pli-tv-bu-pm-sk2), the Bhikkhu Parivāra, and the corresponding rules for nuns in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, and Bhikkhunī Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Beyond the Theravāda tradition, parallels survive in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan within the Vinayas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya schools [SuttaCentral].
